summary.headline: Kilburn Q4 FY26 standalone revenue INR134 crores at 25.1% EBITDA; FY27 guidance 20-25% growth to INR750-800 crores with order intake target INR800-1,000 crores.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 standalone revenue of INR134 crores with 25.1% EBITDA margin and FY26 standalone revenue of INR448 crores at 25.9%. Consolidated FY26 revenue was INR629 crores at 25.13% EBITDA, with Q4 consolidated revenue of INR189 crores at 22.95%, the latter diluted by freight and subcontract costs on a large Moroccan order. Working capital days rose from 169 to 184 and operating cash flow was negative on a standalone basis, which management attributed to heavy dispatches in the last two months of the year. Several large orders slipped by about a quarter due to the Middle East crisis, and the Monga Strayfield dispatches were delayed by logistics constraints.

segments.name: Kilburn Engineering (standalone)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR134 crores at 25.1% EBITDA; standalone trade receivables rose by about INR100 crores in FY26 as Q4 dispatches reached about INR130 crores versus INR50-60 crores a year earlier. Expansion at Saravali plant expected by end Q2 FY27.

segments.name: M.E. Energy (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Phase 2 expansion at Pune expected by end Q2 FY27. Strong ferrous alloy and steel inquiries; cement business mainly hot air generators with repeat orders; first waste heat recovery boiler inquiry in cement at early stage. Quoting jobs above INR300 crores.

segments.name: Monga Strayfield (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue hit by Middle East logistics disruption; ready equipment held in storage awaiting shipping. Management expects catch-up by first half FY27. Revenue split approximately 50:50 between RF dryers and sheet metal, per management range guidance. Short order cycle of about 3 months.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth target 20-25%, implying INR750-800 crores at group level; target to reach INR1,000 crores by FY28.
FY27 group order intake target INR800-1,000 crores; management expects at least INR450-500 crores closed by end Q2 FY27 and INR500-600 crores booked by September.
EBITDA margin guidance 20%+ with management referencing a 22-23% operating range; management said other income (about 80% operating, mainly export FX gains) should be included in EBITDA.
Depreciation expected at INR14-15 crores, rising by a few crores after new capex; finance cost expected to stay broadly stable.
Capex for FY27 around INR40 crores, spread across standalone and subsidiaries; capex programme expected complete by Sept-Oct 2026.
Management sees exports reaching 30-40% of revenue over time.
capex_capacity: Kilburn Saravali factory expansion and M.E. Energy Phase 2 expansion at Pune both expected by end Q2 FY27.
Management says capacity after current expansion is sufficient for INR800 crores of revenue comfortably; further capex needed for growth to FY28 scale.
Office building demolished to make way for a new bay at the factory; INR2-3 crores written off in opex.
Capex programme under implementation expected to complete September-October 2026.
demand_pricing: Inquiry pipeline about INR4,000 crores at consolidated level across fertilizer, nuclear, sludge processing, petrochemicals, offshore gas vapour recovery, steel and ferrous alloy, cement, textiles, food processing and defrosting.
Two nuclear orders in hand, expected to take a year plus to execute; competition mainly from Lloyds Engineering; 2-3 further nuclear projects visible (including Kaiga), via EPC partners.
Several orders expected to close in Q4 FY26 slipped by about a quarter due to Middle East crisis; a Moroccan order of INR50-60 crores receivable in the next 2-3 months.
Material costs rising with steel prices; management says material is booked at order award and cost is not passed through, though prices rise with turnover.
Inquiry ticket sizes: INR2-5 crores for smaller machines, about INR40 crores for some inquiries, and INR100 crores+ for large projects; tea dryers INR40-50 lakhs excluded.

qa_highlights.question: Why has standalone cash flow turned negative and when will operating cash flow turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Vijayakar attributed it to receivables from heavy Q4 dispatches (about INR130 crores versus INR50-60 crores a year earlier); collections expected from June. Consolidated operating cash flow is positive. Working capital days to reduce, but not drastically.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating leverage not show in FY26 and why has PAT lagged revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Amritanshu Khaitan said leverage has already been achieved and margins are stable at about 25%; growth is being reinvested in people, talent and infrastructure. PAT lag reflects full tax from FY26 versus carried-forward losses earlier, plus the INR2-3 crore write-off.

qa_highlights.question: Has the FY27 growth guidance been cut from 25-30% to 20-25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Khaitan said the guidance has always been 20-25% and was not changed; the 25-30% figure in the investor presentation was a typo by the IR team, with the press release showing 20-25%.

qa_highlights.question: Is any further warrant-related dilution expected?
qa_highlights.answer: All warrant conversions have happened; no further dilution expected.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin decline in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Vijayakar said the executing orders had a higher share of outside subcontract charges; margin depends on order mix and equipment type.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management of INR750-800 crores revenue given a tepid opening order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Ranjit Lala said some orders slipped by a quarter and management will revert next quarter if there is deviation; Khaitan said H2 will carry more of the execution weight, assuming orders are finalised in 30-60 days.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a sector or subsidiary breakup of order intake?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a subsidiary or sector order breakup, citing that orders can be executed across plants.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margins recover to 23-25% in FY27-28 with steel prices normalising?
qa_highlights.answer: Khaitan said other income should be included in margin (about 80% operating); quarterly margin is about 23% and full-year consolidated is 25%. Ranjit Lala said costs are not passed through and the normal target range is 20-23%, with 25% possibly not sustainable every year.

risks_watch: Order intake timing: management expects INR450-500 crores closed by end Q2 FY27, against an opening backlog of INR467 crores that management concedes is lower than last year.

Working capital and receivables: standalone receivables rose by about INR100 crores; management expects collections of about INR50-60 crores from the Moroccan order and recovery from June to September.
Middle East crisis effects on shipping lead times, gas availability for production and Monga Strayfield dispatches.
Steel and metal price inflation with no pass-through clause; management books material at order award.
Guidance messaging: the investor presentation showed a 25-30% CAGR typo versus 20-25% in the press release; the IR team should correct the document.
summary.management_tone: Confident on medium-term targets and FY27 execution, but cautious on near-term order intake, which management attributes to geopolitical delays. Management was defensive on margin questions, repeatedly asking analysts to look at annualised and other-income-inclusive margins, and declined to give subsidiary-level order and revenue breakups.
key_quotes: So operating leverage and economies of scale has already played out.
We do not believe in looking at 5-year plans and 10-year plans and working on those kinds of aspirational numbers.
We have not changed that guidance in the current quarter, firstly.

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth target of 20-25% (INR750-800 cr) held, backed by Saravali and Pune expansions due by end Q2 FY27 (capacity said sufficient for INR800 cr) and a group order backlog of INR467 cr, though Q4 orders slipped a quarter and the FY27 order intake target of INR800-1,000 cr is only partly evidenced by specific closings (INR450-500 cr by end Q2).
